name: Prawn Laksa

steps: Pound chilli, lemongrass, ginger, garlic, olive oil, onion, coriander and fish sauce into a paste (pestle & mortar or food processor).
Cook noodles according to packet directions; drain.
Heat a pan, add the paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add prawns and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk, hot water and lime juice; simmer for 5 minutes.
Drain noodles, add to the soup, and serve.

name: Teriyaki Salmon Rice Bowl

ingredients.alt: Swap 1 cup for cauliflower rice — saves roughly 130 kcal and adds fibre

steps: Sprinkle sake over the salmon fillet; set aside.
Thinly shred cabbage and radish; soak in water.
Pat salmon dry, removing excess sake and moisture.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat; pan-fry salmon until cooked through.
Remove salmon and cut into pieces. Wipe the pan, then simmer the teriyaki sauce.
Return salmon to the pan and coat in the teriyaki sauce.
Divide rice between bowls; top with salmon, vegetables, edamame and garnish.

ingredients.alt: Trim any visible fat, or swap 20% of the steak for extra Chinese broccoli to bulk the dish without adding calories
Cut to 1 tsp — saves ~20 kcal
Use 250g noodles + extra Chinese broccoli — saves ~55 kcal

steps: Combine all marinade ingredients with the beef; marinate 15 minutes.
Mix the sauce ingredients in a bowl. Separate fresh noodles gently, or cook dried noodles per packet directions.
Heat a pan or wok over high heat. Sear beef in batches for 2-3 minutes until browned and slightly charred, leaving it untouched for about 1 minute before flipping. Remove from pan.
Add oil, then garlic and ginger paste. Stir-fry 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add Chinese broccoli stems and cook 2 minutes, then add the leaves and cook 1-2 minutes until wilted. Remove from pan.
Add noodles to the hot pan and let sit undisturbed for about 30 seconds to lightly char. Toss gently so they don't break apart. Pour in the sauce and cook 1 minute until evenly coated.
Return beef and vegetables to the pan and toss 1-2 minutes until glossy and combined. Add bean sprouts and spring onions during the last 30 seconds.
Serve immediately, topped with chili oil and chili flakes if desired.

ingredients.n: Pandan leaves, tied in a knot

ingredients.n: Chinese rice wine (Shaoxing Hua Tiao, optional)

steps: Marinate the chicken breasts with salt and sesame oil for 15-30 minutes (no need for the multi-hour marinate a whole chicken needs).
Place shallots, garlic, ginger, pandan leaves and cooking oil in the mixing bowl. Sauté 8 min/120°C/speed 1. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

Place chicken stock in the mixing bowl. Insert the simmering basket, add rice and the reserved aromatic oil. Place the marinated chicken breasts in the Varoma dish and position on the lid; steam 15 min/Varoma/speed 3.
Check chicken is cooked through (internal temp 75°C+); if needed, steam a further 2-3 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes.
Meanwhile mix a little reserved stock with the soy sauce, sugar and rice wine in a bowl.
Slice the chicken, drizzle with the sauce, and serve with the rice and sliced cucumber.

name: Spinach Ohitashi
timeNote: Needs at least 1 hour to chill/soak in the dashi before serving (not counted in cook time) — plan ahead, or serve right after blanching if you're short on time.
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil; blanch spinach for 30-60 seconds until just wilted. Transfer to ice water, then squeeze out excess liquid and cut into thirds.
Combine kombu and water; let steep 5 minutes (or use a quick dashi). Stir in mirin and soy sauce.
Soak the spinach in the dashi mixture for at least 1 hour in the fridge (can serve sooner if pressed for time, though flavor is best after resting).
Drain lightly, plate, and top with sesame seeds and bonito flakes if using.
